question: Dark patches on the sun are referred to as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**sunspots**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Dark patches on the sun are called sunspots: 
 
• Sunspots are cooler regions on the sun's surface that appear dark because they are surrounded by a hotter surface.
 
• They are caused by intense magnetic fields that inhibit the flow of hot gas from the sun's interior to the surface. 
 
• Sunspots can be the size of planets. They are typically made up of a dark center called the umbra and a lighter outer region called the penumbra. 
 
• Sunspots have magnetic fields that are thousands of times stronger than Earth's.
 
• These magnetic fields can create active regions on the sun that can lead to solar flares and coronal mass ejections. 
 
• Sunspots can look like specks on the sun's surface. 
 
• One theory for how sunspots are created is that the sun's rotation causes the magnetic field to become "wound up".
 
• This stretching creates tubes in the magnetic field that break the surface and create areas of lower temperature
